answer: A stake-weighted reputation ridge makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock quartz-hard collateral that decays only after a long honest history, so creating many fake identities multiplies cost instead of influence. A willow-flexible decay schedule lets genuine newcomers earn trust gradually, while a sudden burst of new accounts faces steep collateral and slow reputation growth. Attackers must therefore fund every identity for months before it can sway decisions, raising the price of a Sybil swarm above any gain from gaming the vote.
